messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — since this morning we're seeing a cluster-wide spike in GPU pod evictions on the g4dn-heavy pool. Evictions correlate with NIC errors on a subset of nodes and some preemptions when the scheduler tries to binpack. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:
Ajay Patel: saw a handful. evicted pods show kubelet eviction reason: 'memory pressure' and also some 'NodeLease' disconnects. Can you paste kubectl describe of an evicted pod?
Maria Chen: sure, here's one snippet:
```
Name:         model-infer-84d9c
Namespace:    prod
Reason:       Evicted
Message:      The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage.
```
But on the nodes I also see mlx5 NIC WARNs and packet drops in dmesg.
Serena Li: this smells like two problems colliding: 1) network flakiness causing kubelet retries/disconnects -> eviction, 2) binpacking behavior causing smaller GPU requests to fragment capacity so when a big job schedules it preempts others.
Tom Garcia: fwiw our device-plugin prevents fractional GPUs, so lots of 1-GPU pods on 8-GPU machines will leave fragmentation if requests vary.
Kevin O'Neill: agree. Also flagged that node labels for 'gpu-class=highmem' vs 'gpu-class=balanced' are inconsistent; scheduler scoring might be preferring cheap nodes which have NIC contention.
Ajay Patel: InfraBot just ran a quick descheduler check and found many low-priority cron inference pods sitting on packed nodes. InfraBot: descheduler run scheduled at 2026-03-18T09:10Z, candidate evictions: 72 pods (low priority/long lived).
Maria Chen: possible short-term mitigations: add a toleration for a 'packing' taint to mark binpack-friendly pods, and create a dedicated "large-model" nodepool with 8x A100-ish instances so big jobs don't scatter.
Serena Li: also consider topologySpreadConstraints or preferredPodAffinity to keep same model shards together. Example: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution for podAffinity to prefer same-node placement.
Tom Garcia: patch suggestion: enable scheduler plugin 'NodeResourcesFit' + custom scoring to favor packing GPUs by available gpus descending. We can test in staging by flipping scoringWeight for GPU count.
Kevin O'Neill: another angle — NIC errors. If Mellanox/eni firmware causing packet loss under high TX bursts, packing many GPU pods on same NIC can exacerbate. Ops: can we throttle outgoing traffic per pod or move high-throughput pods to different AZs?
Ajay Patel: I'll run a staged change: 1) bring up a 16-node 'large-model' pool (p4d-ish), 2) deploy scheduler scoring tweak in staging, 3) enable descheduler nightly evictions for low-priority pods. Will monitor evictions and NIC errors.
Maria Chen: temporary toleration + nodeSelector example to force onto large pool:
```
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    rpool: large-model
  tolerations:
  - key: "node-role.kubernetes.io/large"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Serena Li: long term we should: a) consolidate small-request workloads into a dedicated packed pool, b) reserve a small fraction of nodes for noise isolation (NIC heavy), c) refine autoscaler scalingPolicy to prefer adding homogeneous nodes to avoid mixed-instance fragmentation.
Tom Garcia: +1. Also queueing: make low-priority jobs preemptible with graceful drain so we don't get abrupt evictions that kill in-flight batches. Add a preemption grace period annotation.
Kevin O'Neill: cost check — moving to larger instances will increase unit costs but reduces eviction thrash. Run a cost vs. eviction-thrash calc before prod rollout. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Maria Chen: agreed — I'll open an RFC with the pilot plan and cost estimate. Ajay, assign staging tasks?
Ajay Patel: on it. I'll post results by EOD. :eyes:
InfraBot: Incident ticket #INF-2026-112 created for tracking. Will post updates here.
